reading: The 3x3 input becomes a 5x5 grid of 3x3 blocks: the centre 3x3 blocks are the input scaled x3 (each coloured cell a solid block); for every coloured input cell on the input's edge, a copy of the input is placed in the outer block just beyond it in each outward direction (corner cells give two copies).

slots.centre: input upscaled x3 placed at block offset (1,1)
slots.copies: input copy in the block adjacent outward from each edge fg cell (up/down/left/right only, no diagonals)

why: every 3x3 block is empty, solid fg colour, or an exact input copy, as dictated by the input's cells

reading: Each colour-4 shape touching a vertical colour-2 wall is reflected across the wall to the other side, and the reflection is painted in the colour of the single marker cell on that side.

slots.subject: 4-shape adjacent to a vertical 2 segment
slots.colour: colour of the marker cell lying inside the reflected footprint

why: the new cells are exactly the mirror image of the 4-shape about the wall, in the marker's colour

reading: Noise 8 cells inside the 2 area become 2; each 8 cell inside the 7 area gains one more 8 cell next to it on the side facing the colour-9 border line.

slots.grow: 8 cells in the 7 area -> also paint the neighbour one step toward the 9 edge line

why: only 8 cells and their one neighbour toward the 9 line change

reading: From each 6 on the bottom row a path is drawn upward in 2; when it meets a horizontal 7 bar from below it marks the bar cell 8, turns and runs under the bar (4 at the turn, 2 along, 3 at the corner past the bar's end) and continues up, ending in a 6 at the top or in a gap of a bar.

slots.turn: run right under the bar to one past its end
slots.marks: 8 on the bar cell hit, 4 at the turn start, 3 at the turn end, 2 for the path, 6 at the path end

why: the path never crosses a 7 bar; each bar it meets is passed on its right end
invariants: all 7 cells kept except the hit cell becomes 8

reading: Crop the rectangle marked by the four 4 corner cells; inside it, the partial scaled-up pieces are completed into a full scaled copy of the small multi-coloured key shape found elsewhere.

slots.crop: box spanned by the four 4 corner cells
slots.key: small multi-colour component outside the box
slots.scale: factor given by the size of the pieces inside the box
slots.placement: aligned so the existing pieces match the scaled key

why: the output is the corner box with the scaled key drawn so all existing coloured pieces agree with it

reading: For each non-background colour, its cell count N (a square number) becomes a solid sqrt(N) x sqrt(N) square; the squares are laid out left to right in increasing size, bottom-aligned, separated by one background column, output height = largest side.

slots.per colour: number of cells of that colour

why: each output square's area equals the input count of its colour

reading: Each solid rectangle has one odd-coloured cell at an inner corner; the rectangle's interior (inside its 1-cell border) is cleared to background and diagonals are drawn from all four interior corners toward the centre in the odd cell's colour.

slots.subject: each solid rectangle
slots.pattern: X of diagonals from the four interior corners, each running inward until the middle

why: border ring of each rectangle unchanged; interior holds only the diagonal X

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled into a 9x9 grid of 3x3 blocks; the blocks at the input's background positions get the colour-inverted input (fg<->bg), the others stay empty.

slots.unit: input with fg and bg swapped

why: each block is the inverted input where the input cell is background, else empty

reading: The grid has three 3x3 panels separated by 5 columns; the second panel is filled with the first panel rotated 90 degrees clockwise and the third with the first rotated 180 degrees.
why: panels 2 and 3 are exact rotations of panel 1
invariants: panel 1 and the 5 separator columns unchanged

reading: The 8 shapes sit in 4x4 boxes (grid anchored at the top-left of all fg); every background cell in a box that contains 8 is filled with 2.

new_rows.name: boxbg
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
fy0(C, min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
fx0(C, min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
by0(Y) :- fy0(C, Y).
by0(Y2) :- by0(Y), Y2 = Y + 4, px(Y2, X, C).
bx0(X) :- fx0(C, X).
bx0(X2) :- bx0(X), X2 = X + 4, px(Y, X2, C).
inblk(Y, X, BY, BX) :- by0(BY), bx0(BX), px(Y, X, C), Y >= BY, Y3 = BY + 3, Y <= Y3, X >= BX, X3 = BX + 3, X <= X3.
blkfg(BY, BX) :- inblk(Y, X, BY, BX), isfg(Y, X).
boxbg(Y, X) :- inblk(Y, X, BY, BX), blkfg(BY, BX), !isfg(Y, X).

why: every background cell in a 4x4 box holding 8 becomes 2; nothing else changes
